definitions.explanation: The day in spring when day and night are approximately equal in length, occurring around March 20-21 in the Northern Hemisphere. Also refers to the associated seasonal period in the traditional calendar.

examples.japanese: {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ}は{祝日|しゅくじつ}だ。
examples.english: The Vernal Equinox Day is a national holiday.

examples.japanese: {春分|しゅんぶん}を{過|す}ぎると、{昼|ひる}が{長|なが}くなる。
examples.english: After the spring equinox, the days get longer.

examples.japanese: {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ}には、{家族|かぞく}でお{墓参|はかまい}りに{行|い}く{習慣|しゅうかん}がある。
examples.english: There is a custom of visiting family graves on the Vernal Equinox Day.

notes:
{春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ} (Vernal Equinox Day) is a Japanese national holiday, typically on March 20 or 21. It falls during {春|はる}の{彼岸|ひがん} (spring equinox week), a Buddhist period for visiting family graves and honoring ancestors. Traditional foods include ぼた{餅|もち} (rice cakes coated in sweet bean paste).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ}: Vernal Equinox Day (national holiday)
- {春分|しゅんぶん}{点|てん}: vernal equinox point (astronomy)

RELATED WORDS:
- {秋分|しゅうぶん}: autumnal equinox
- {彼岸|ひがん}: equinox period (Buddhist observance)
- {夏至|げし}: summer solstice
- {冬至|とうじ}: winter solstice
